posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked:
I find when I'm working on a custom deck (I do a lot of that?), I want to have a theme and/or a mechanic in mind first.  Then develop it from there.  To keep Captain Thunder from being like Legacy, find a mechanic or theme that fits him well and use that.  Legacy was one of the first decks, so his mechanic isn't super-amazing, but his theme is about support and tanking, with some damage thrown on top.  Captain Thunder will have all the years of previous deck building experience to help come up with a mechanic there, and all the backstory for a theme.

There are a bunch of different ways to view any particular theme or ability.  In RPGS, speedsters can be designed by actually having a high speed attribute or by having abilities that act much like having a high speed would, but without actually increasing that speed (Area attacks representing punching all the things, high movement (not the same as high speed as they can't take more actions per round), improved accuracy, improved defenses, etc.

Hopefully this helps shed a little light on how Captain Thunder can be like Legacy without being like Legacy.

Yeah, I think Sentinels players and fans are definitely part of the target audience.

That said I think we'll see more information about the heroes and villains and environments that will be in the core boxed set as the kickstarter progresses. There's plenty of time for updates to answer questions and concerns.

That said

Captain Thunder is similar to Legacy + having lightning powers. He gained his powers while flying through a hurricane, after multiple lightning bolts struck the cockpit. His role is as senior statesman and leader of the Freedom League.

Daedalus is an immortal inventor - literally the mythical figure as in Daedalus and Icarus - who fights crime in an Iron Man-like battlesuit

Dr. Metropolis is basically the avatar of Freedom City, and I think the closest any character from comics comes is Jack Hawksmoor of Stormwatch/Authority.

Johnny Rocket is a speedster, and the grandchild of the original Johnny Rocket (the powers skipped a generation). Also, Johnny's another gay speedster, which I only mention because Tachyon's a lesbian.

Lady Liberty is a legacy character, going back to the American Revolutionary War. That is there have been several women who have been empowered by the Spirit of Liberty and taken up the mantle. This is of course not quite the same kind of legacy as Legacy, since they're not typically related. On Earth-Prime, one Lady Liberty was the inspiration for the Statue of Liberty.

Pseudo is an alien, formerly a citizen of the Grue Unity, an interstellar empire that was planning to invade Earth. Grue came to Earth to warn humanity and joined the Freedom League to help fight off the invasion. He was originally a scout and infiltrator intended to prepare the way for the Grue Unity to invade other civilizations, but his time among humans taught him compassion and empathy.

Raven is a second-generation superhero. Her father was the original Raven, although he retired from superheroing to raise a family. When his daughter was kidnapped by his own father, Dr. Sin, he reassumed the mantle of Raven and set out to rescue her. His daughter, post-rescue, decided she wanted to take on his role as a crimefighter. She did this despite the fact that her father was against this.

Siren is empowered by a voudoun loa, Siren (yes an actual loa from the tradition), and has power over the sea and sea life. Basically, Siren wants to prove that humanity is worth saving, while apparently Baron Samedi feels differently. Each chose a representative to prove their case, and Siren (the heroine) was Siren (the loa's) choice.

Star Knight is a police officer who was recruited into an intersteller organization called the "Star Knights." They have more in common with the Green Lantern Corps than anything, although they have technologically advanced battlesuits rather than power rings.

I mean these aren't much just what I could come up with offhand.

Omega rules The Terminus. The Terminus is basically the end of all things, but it has elements similar to Jack Kirby's 4th World. From The Terminus Omega invades other worlds in order to basically annihilate them. One of his plots was to annihilate the "Omniverse" which is just the word for the multiverse in which Freedom City exists. Omega represents an existential threat to all life.

Farside City is a city on the dark side of the moon inhabited by humans with psionic powers. Yes this is kind of a take on the Inhumans, but it is its own thing as well.

Tartarus is what it says on the tin. Hades is in charge (the mythological Hades).

Freedom City is similar to Metropolis or Megalopolis, but has its own things too, that I am utterly failing to remember properly.

The Meta-Mind is the ruler of the Grue Unity and wants to subjugate basically everything.

Argo is an android that was designed to mimic superpowers, but during his encounter with the Freedom League was locked into having their powers and their powers only. This only leaves him overwhelmingly powerful (like, more powerful than Omega if you straight up compare the two) instead of potentially omnipotent.

I plan to back Sentinels of Earth Prime.  Payday is Tuesday, so I have to wait till then.

What do I want to see?  I'd like to see some general design notes:  how is Bowman going to differ from Expatriette, in terms of "shock arrow/bullets, ice arrow/bullets, fire arrow/bullets"?  What does Lady Liberty bring to the table?  What mechanics are being experimented with, which we haven't seen before?

On the topic of double-standards for what content was desired for deciding whether or not to purchase SotM vs. what content is being voiced as desired/necessary for deciding whether or not to purchase SoEP, I think a significant difference is that the core game for SotM was not made available via Kickstarter. Anyone backing a SotM kickstarter for a later expansion would have had the opportunity to see that the decks from the previous SotM releases were of a certain quality, in terms of art, in terms of mechanics, in terms of story/character/style/feel. 

As a SotM fan, but not familiar with M&M, I have confidence in the mechanics of the proposed SoEP decks, since Christopher is making them, but don't have much to go on in terms of judging the art, story, character, style, feel, etc. I _could_ go out and peruse a bunch (a whole bunch, I gather) of M&M Lore and art, but that would be both rather a lot of effort and also risk that whatever I find won't be a represenative slice of what will make it into _this_ game, into _this_ representation of these characters and places. So, instead, I'd like to see the Kickstarter campaign give me enough of a taste of these things to make a judgement about these sort of things. 

If there are later Kickstarters for SoEP expansions, I don't think there will be the same strong need to see as much about the art, characters, story, etc. because people will have formed an opinion about whether or not decks from this game are the kind of thing they like.

On the topic of whether or not the people on this form represent a significant enough slice of the market for SoEP to be valuable to invest effort into: Interesting question! Around here I think it's easy to think that we're more important than we are -- many of us seem to be thinking about SotM all the time. I'm not sure, though, that we are either a particularly large slice of people interested in SotM or particularly representative of many people who are interested in SotM. Maybe, but I'm not so sure. Still, my guess is that it's worth Green Ronin's time to come here and start a conversation about what this community would be excited to see and support. I'm not sure why they haven't done that. My guess is that there's just too much to do and they simply can't do everything that would be cool.
